cells.document: A Statement of the Traditional Southern Baptist Understanding of God's Plan of Salvation
cells.date: 2012 (text as published in The Alabama Baptist, 21 June 2012)
cells.section: Article Eight: The Free Will of Man (affirmation); see also the denials of Article Four and Article Five
cells.excerpt: endows each person with actual free will (the ability to choose between two options)
cells.shows: The signers affirm that each person has a free will that must be exercised in accepting or rejecting God's call, and they deny that grace cannot be resisted or that anyone is regenerated before responding to the gospel.
cells.binding_note: Representative, not binding: a statement signed by individual Southern Baptist pastors, professors and leaders. It was never adopted by the Convention.

cells.section: Article V, God's Purpose of Grace
cells.excerpt: It is consistent with the free agency of man, and comprehends all the means in connection with the end.
cells.shows: The Convention's confession says election is consistent with human free agency without defining how; Calvinist and non-Calvinist Southern Baptists both subscribe to this article.
cells.binding_note: The Convention's adopted confession. Shared by both Southern Baptist wings, so it does not by itself place this wing at 80.

cells.section: Article VII, Baptism and the Lord's Supper
cells.excerpt: The Lord's Supper is a symbolic act of obedience
cells.shows: The article calls baptism the immersion of a believer and an act of obedience symbolizing faith, and says that in the Supper church members memorialize the death of the Redeemer and anticipate his second coming.

cells.document: Statement of the Board of Trustees, Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary (as quoted in Baptist Press, 'SWBTS takes stance against Pentecostal/charismatic doctrine', Tammi Reed Ledbetter, posted 17 October 2006)
cells.excerpt: will not knowingly endorse in any way, advertise, or commend the conclusions of the contemporary charismatic movement
cells.shows: The trustees of one Convention seminary, then led by a prominent non-Calvinist president, declined to endorse the charismatic movement or private prayer language and said they would not hire faculty who promote them.
cells.binding_note: Representative at most, not binding: an institutional policy of one seminary's trustees, read through a news report and not the original minute. It rejects charismatic practice; it does not state that the sign gifts have ceased. The Baptist Faith and Message 2000 says nothing on spiritual gifts or tongues, so no Convention-wide document exists for this cell. The live baptistpress.com page returned 403 to automated fetches; the text was read from the Wayback Machine copy.

cells.excerpt: Jesus Christ will return personally and visibly in glory to the earth
cells.shows: The confession affirms Christ's personal, visible return, the resurrection and the judgment, and takes no position on the millennium, the rapture, or a distinct future for national Israel.
cells.binding_note: The confession is deliberately silent on the question this axis measures. No confession, resolution or representative body statement placing non-Calvinist Southern Baptists on the dispensational side was found; for a document that states the dispensational lean, the answer is: none found.

cells.section: Preamble, point (4) (carried over from the 1925 statement); see also Article I, The Scriptures
cells.excerpt: The sole authority for faith and practice among Baptists is the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments.
cells.shows: The preamble names Scripture as the sole authority and calls confessions only guides in interpretation with no authority over the conscience; Article I calls Scripture the supreme standard by which creeds and religious opinions are tried.

cells.section: Article VI, The Church (first paragraph); see also Article VIII, The Lord's Day
cells.excerpt: an autonomous local congregation of baptized believers, associated by covenant in the faith and fellowship of the gospel
cells.shows: The confession makes each local congregation autonomous, governed by Christ's laws and observing two ordinances, and Article VIII asks only that the Lord's Day include exercises of worship; it prescribes no liturgy or calendar.
cells.binding_note: Free worship is implied by congregational autonomy and by the absence of any prescribed order; the confession never discusses liturgy directly.

notes: All excerpts were copied from pages opened on 2026-09-19. The Baptist Faith and Message 2000 and the 2012 Traditional Statement are in copyright, so every excerpt is under 20 words and marked link only. The Baptist Faith and Message text was read through a fetch tool that returns page text (a direct curl of bfm.sbc.net returned only a stub), so a human should eyeball the excerpts against the live page before publication; the Traditional Statement and Baptist Press excerpts were confirmed by grepping the raw downloaded HTML. The Baptist Faith and Message is shared by Calvinist and non-Calvinist Southern Baptists, so only the grace axis has a document peculiar to this wing, and that document is a signed statement, not a Convention action. Its signers call their view 'Traditional' and the text does not use the word 'synergist'; the site should not put that label in their mouths. Gifts: the International Mission Board adopted a guideline in November 2005 excluding candidates who practise a private prayer language and, per press reports seen in search results only (not opened), dropped it in 2015; it was not cited because its text could not be opened (baptistpress.com and baptiststandard.com returned 403). Kingdom: an SBC Life symposium ('Southern Baptists and the Millennium', David Roach, posted 1 June 2014, Baptist Press, read via the Wayback Machine) confirms that 'the BF&M does not address the millennium' and prints Southern Baptist contributors holding traditional dispensational, progressive dispensational, historic premillennial and amillennial views side by side; it is a magazine feature by individual authors, not a body's statement, so it is recorded here as context and not as a citation. The coordinates of 75 on gifts and 72 on kingdom therefore rest on observed practice, not on any document this tradition has adopted.
